# Hood struts installation

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Attach hood strut mounting brackets, drill and tap holes, then secure them with screws. [t1686]

[Partial] Select a gas spring with an appropriate weight rating and mount brackets to the hood. [t1686]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Select a gas spring with the appropriate weight rating, such as 67 lbs or 90 lbs.
2. [Partial] Mount brackets to the hood and fender using self-tapping screws if drilling is not desired.

_Procedure reported by [t1686]._

## Tools

- Drill [t1686]
- Drill bit (correct size for tap) [t1686]
- Tap [t1686]
- Fine point sharpie [t1686]
- Screwdriver or nutdriver [t1686]
- Center punch [t1686]

## Parts

- [Partial] Brackets: Often sold as part of a kit or sourced separately, e.g., Austin Hardware. [t1686]
- Gas spring, e.g., Stabilus Genesis, Strongarm: Weight ratings vary from 22.5 lbs to 90 lbs; 67 lbs is a common choice. [t1686]
- [Partial] Hood struts: 90 lbs of force each, 60 lb also acceptable [t1686]
- Mounting brackets: 4 pieces, 90-degree style with a 10mm ball [t1686]
- Screws: 16 total; size depends on bracket holes chosen [t1686]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Start by mounting the bottom brackets before attaching struts to simplify alignment. [t1686]
- Orient the 90-degree brackets carefully to find a good flat surface for contact. [t1686]
- Pilot holes are recommended when using self-tapping screws to prevent stripping. [t1686]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using struts that are too light, resulting in one strut failing to hold the hood up while two work well together. [t1686]
